eval12@01cfbb1e713f-6ec8137fd3.question: Join each invoice line item to its order item (order item id of the order item equals order item id of the invoice line), then to its order (order id equal), then to its customer (customer id equal). Each join gives one row per match and drops lines with no match. Group by the invoice line's order item id and customer town or city. For each group compute: (a) the plain average of the stored product price per unit (Invoice_Line_Items.product_price) values, used as stored with no division by quantity or anything else; and (b) the average of A ÷ B, where A is Invoice_Line_Items.derived_product_cost (the line product cost) and B is the line total cost including VAT. Missing values are ignored in both averages (missing when there are none). Then group those group rows by town or city. For each town compute P, the average of the group values (a), and R, the average of the group values (b). Missing values are ignored (missing when there are none). Next compute Q, the average of R over all towns (missing values ignored; missing when there are none). Pair each town row with Q, keeping only towns where it is not true that Q is missing (one row per match; towns with no match are left out). Keep only towns where R is greater than Q. Return, in this order: the town or city, P, R, and R − Q.

Missing values are ignored in both averages (missing when there are none). Then group those group rows by town or city. For each town, compute P, the average of the group average prices, and R, the average of the group cost ratio averages. Missing values are ignored (missing when there are none). Next, compute Q, the average of R over all towns (missing values ignored). Pair each town row with Q, keeping only towns where it is not true that Q is missing (one row per match; towns with no match are left out). Keep only towns where R is greater than Q. Return, in this order: the town or city, P, R, and R − Q.

failures.reason: READ-BACK: a careful reader, given only this question, the schema and the documentation, wrote the SQL below. Its answer differs from the answer the requirements define. Find which requirement the question states differently, names wrongly (for example a column number of an earlier step), or leaves open, and fix only that. The reader's SQL: WITH g AS (SELECT oi.order_item_id, c.town_city, AVG(CAST(ili.product_price AS REAL) / NULLIF(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS REAL), 0)) AS avg_price, AVG(CAST(ili.derived_product_cost AS REAL) / NULLIF(CAST(ili.derived_total_cost AS REAL), 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili JOIN Order_Items oi ON ili.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id JOIN Orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY oi.order_item_id, c.town_city), t AS (SELECT town_city, AVG(avg_price) AS P, AVG(avg_ratio) AS R FROM g GROUP BY town_city), q AS (SELECT AVG(R) AS Q FROM t) SELECT t.town_city, t.P, t.R, t.R - q.Q FROM t JOIN q ON q.Q IS NOT NULL WHERE t.R > q.Q
